root_cause.text: The cdns3 gadget endpoint queue path (`__cdns3_gadget_ep_queue()` in `drivers/usb/cdns3/cdns3-gadget.c`) dereferenced `ep->desc` without first verifying that the endpoint was configured/enabled, so calling `ep_queue` on an unconfigured endpoint could hit a NULL pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!ep->desc) return -ESHUTDOWN;` at the start of `__cdns3_gadget_ep_queue()`, and the CVE description states that `ep->desc` can be NULL when the gadget endpoint is disabled or not yet configured, leading to a NULL pointer dereference and crash.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject gadget endpoint queue operations when the endpoint is not configured by returning -ESHUTDOWN early.
intent_record.what: A null/absence check was added at the start of __cdns3_gadget_ep_queue(): if ep->desc is not set, the function now returns -ESHUTDOWN before touching the request fields or proceeding with queueing.
intent_record.how: At runtime, endpoint queueing is now rejected when the endpoint is not enabled/configured (no descriptor present), preventing requests from being queued against an inactive endpoint and avoiding invalid state transitions.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by preventing endpoint queue operations unless the endpoint is configured/enabled, avoiding the NULL dereference of ep->desc.

candidates.rationale: This is part of the pre-fix queue path that proceeds without any early validation that the endpoint is configured/enabled. In the vulnerable flow, execution continued past this point into logic that dereferenced ep->desc, allowing a NULL pointer dereference when ep_queue was called on an unconfigured endpoint.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line is in the unguarded gadget endpoint queue path that lacked an early check for whether the endpoint was configured/enabled. Because execution continued past this point into code that dereferenced ep->desc, calling ep_queue on an unconfigured endpoint could trigger a NULL pointer dereference.
